text:
I had a very disappointing experience at this hospital during a recent visit to obtain a medical certificate for visa purposes.

During registration, I asked whether they required my social security card for their records. The staff member initially assumed I was referring to payment and told me it would be cash only. I clarified that I was not asking about payment, but whether the card was needed for registration. Despite this, the situation escalated unnecessarily. Another staff member was called over, and I was incorrectly described as trying to use a social security card to avoid paying. I had to repeat myself to clarify that this was not the case.

Although that misunderstanding was eventually acknowledged, the overall interaction left me feeling uncomfortable and misrepresented.

The situation worsened during a routine blood pressure check. I was still processing what had just happened and felt confused. Instead of guiding me calmly, the nurse became impatient and physically pulled my arm into position in a rough manner, which I found inappropriate and unprofessional.

The entire experience felt disorganized, lacking in clear communication, and unnecessarily stressful. I chose this hospital for its convenience, but based on this experience, I would not return.

At the Rajavet hospital I am very satisfied with the result of my silicone nose surgery. Everything went well and I am very happy with the outcome. I would also like to thank Maung Thant Sin Aung for helping with the language and other necessary arrangements at the hospital. I am also very grateful to the doctor and the nurses for their patience and kind care. I am truly happy to receive such excellent service. Thank you very much.

After a very bad fall that resulted in a double ankle fracture, I was rushed to Rajavej Hospital Chiang Mai — and from the very first moment, I knew I was in good hands.
I was taken almost immediately for X-rays and quickly admitted. The efficiency and professionalism of the team were incredibly reassuring during such a stressful time. I underwent ankle surgery to repair the two fractures, and throughout the entire process, my doctor was not only highly skilled but also genuinely caring and attentive.
I was hospitalized for nine days, and I can honestly say my recovery has been excellent. Every nurse, doctor, assistant, and staff member treated me with warmth, compassion, and respect. They made me feel as comfortable and “at home” as one possibly can in a hospital setting.
Pain management was handled perfectly — I received all the medications I needed to stay comfortable. The team also started physiotherapy promptly, helping me regain mobility, learn to walk with crutches, and prepare safely for my flight back home.
What truly touched me was the level of care beyond medical treatment. The hospital provided everything necessary for my journey home and even arranged transportation to the airport. That level of service speaks volumes.
While the hospital building may not be as new as some others in Chiang Mai, the quality of care and service is absolutely impeccable. In the end, it’s the people who make the difference — and the people here are exceptional.
Thank you to all the nurses, assistants, doctors, and administrators. I will carry your kindness and dedication in my heart always.

I did a medical check-up package for my age group. The process was straightforward and typical. The hospital is well maintained and the staff are nice. Afterwards, you get a consultation with the on-duty doctor who explain your results and answers your questions.

Burmese translators are available on-site. Ko Thant Zin Aung was especially helpful.

SSO/Thai social security insurance:

I’m writing this to help other foreigners who have chosen this as their hospital. You can only use your SSO insurance at the one hospital that you chose (from my understanding and experience). You need to go through the main entrance and on the right side there’s a hall leading to the SSO intake area. You can show your insurance card and passport to the queue to the left when you walk. They will take your weight and blood pressure and you sit down with the slip, waiting for them to call your name. After they call your name, describe your symptoms. Sometimes it’s easier to use Google translation if you cannot speak Thai. It also helps them understand more thoroughly. They will then give you a queue to see an English speaking doctor. Just wait for them to call your number or your name again. They have always been helpful for me, although not much help addressing root issues. Rather they are quick to give out medication from the pharmacy. I saw the Physio here as well. They were mildly helpful but SSO only covered for two sessions.

Orthopedic doctor:

Pakpoom Poomcharoen

You will need to see general doctors first to schedule an appointment for a couple weeks out. They won’t ask your availability, just give you the next open time slot and date. I saw him for an ATFL tear in my ankle. His English was very good and he was very thorough and patient. He took the time to explain everything, draw diagrams, show me scans, give me detailed procedure to follow. I genuinely recommend him. Also, he explained that I could only do an X-ray and could not get an MRI. You can only get an MRI covered by SSO if it’s an ongoing, chronic issue lasting several months, for my specific injury. The X-ray was covered.
